name: Storage
tagline: Azure Blob and Amazon S3 that keep every object, link and event, and fail exactly when you ask.
point: SharedKey and SAS for Blob; SigV4 and presigned URLs for S3

capabilities.title: Objects with their history
capabilities.text: Accounts, containers, block and multipart uploads. Each object shows versions, metadata and who wrote it: the app, you, the seed or an agent.

capabilities.title: Wait for the upload
capabilities.text: wait_for_object returns the first new object under a prefix, so a test acts in the app and then waits for the file instead of sleeping.

capabilities.title: Rules per operation
capabilities.text: When put, get, delete, list or link matches account, container and path glob: answer 503, 403, timeout or truncate. First N, every time or a share.

capabilities.title: Try a rule first
capabilities.text: test_rule replays the last requests and shows what each attempt would get, before anything is saved.

capabilities.title: Links you can break
capabilities.text: Every SAS or presigned URL is listed with what it allows, validity and uses. Make its next use expired, badly signed, IP-denied or gone.

capabilities.title: Events like the cloud
capabilities.text: BlobCreated and BlobDeleted in Event Grid or S3 format, to a webhook or a queue, with the Event Grid validation handshake first.

capabilities.title: Break event delivery
capabilities.text: Hold, duplicate, reorder, drop or strip a field from the next event, then resend it to check the app's handler is idempotent.

capabilities.title: Keys and reachability
capabilities.text: rotate_key makes apps that sign with the old key get 403. set_account_reachability makes the whole account time out, 503 or 401.

capabilities.title: Back to the seed
capabilities.text: reset_to_seed puts every account back to its seed folder and says what changed since it was loaded.

excerpts.title: Objects, the next read and the history

callouts.title: Written by the app
callouts.text: Uploaded by acme-api over the real Blob API: size, type, reads and who wrote it.

callouts.title: A read armed to fail
callouts.text: set_next_read makes the next read answer 403, 404, 503, slow, truncated or with a bad MD5.

callouts.title: Added by you
callouts.text: put_object can store a truncated file on purpose; it is never shown as sent by the app.

callouts.title: Next read, per object
callouts.text: Normal by default; pick a failure once, then it goes back to normal by itself.

callouts.title: Versions
callouts.text: Every version is kept, with ETag and Content-MD5, so you can compare what the app overwrote.

excerpts.title: A rule, tried before it is saved

callouts.title: Rules in order
callouts.text: The first rule that matches answers. Each shows its hits today and switches off with one click.

callouts.title: Path glob
callouts.text: Operation, account, container and a glob: * is one level, ** any depth.

callouts.title: The answer
callouts.text: 503, 403, 404, 409, 412, 413, timeout, reset, empty, slow, truncate or bad_md5.

callouts.title: How often
callouts.text: The first N attempts, every time, or a random share of the requests.

callouts.title: What the app will see
callouts.text: Each attempt against the last 50 real requests: 503, 503, then 201.

callouts.title: By state
callouts.text: Valid, expired or revoked; filter by who issued the link and by kind (Azure SAS or S3 presigned).

callouts.title: Refused uses
callouts.text: A late use of an expired link still shows up, with the answer the app's user got.

callouts.title: Revoked
callouts.text: revoke_link: the next use answers 403 AuthenticationFailed, like Azure after a key rotation.

callouts.title: Next use
callouts.text: set_next_use: expired, bad_signature, ip_denied, permission, not_yet_valid or gone.

callouts.title: Uses
callouts.text: Each download with method, status and address, so you see who used the link and when.

provoke.name: Uploads fail twice
provoke.what: 503 on the first 2 PUTs to contracts/**, then 201

provoke.name: Reads fail at random
provoke.what: A share of GETs answer 503 or time out

provoke.name: One bad read
provoke.what: The next read is 403, 404, 503, slow, truncated or bad MD5

provoke.name: Link expired early
provoke.what: The next use of a link answers as expired or badly signed

provoke.name: Link revoked
provoke.what: 403 AuthenticationFailed; the app is not told

provoke.name: Old key
provoke.what: Apps signing with the previous key get 403

provoke.name: Account down
provoke.what: The whole account times out, answers 503 or 401

provoke.name: Events out of order
provoke.what: Reorder, hold for 30 s or drop the next event

provoke.name: Event missing a field
provoke.what: The payload lacks a field the handler expects

advantages.title: Failures the cloud won't give
advantages.text: Azure and S3 do not fail on demand. Here a 503 on the second upload, a truncated read or a late event happens on the next call.

advantages.title: Links you can inspect
advantages.text: Every SAS and presigned URL the app makes is listed with its uses and refusals, which the real portal never shows.

advantages.title: No account, no bill
advantages.text: No subscription, no keys to protect and no egress cost. Each environment has its own accounts and resets to a seed.

advantages.title: Proof of who wrote what
advantages.text: Objects remember whether the app, a test, an agent or the seed wrote them, so a test can prove the app did the upload.

agent.prompt: Make the contract upload fail twice with 503 and check that the app retries and the object ends up in storage.
